water.eto_source_note: ETo = FAO-56 Penman-Monteith (eq. 6) with ECCC station Tmax/Tmin (mean of Salmon Arm CS 116FRMN and Silver Creek 1167337, which closed in 2021; POWER on days neither reports) and POWER radiation, humidity (ea, eq. 19) and wind. The POWER cell sits at about 1,025 m against a field at about 450 m, so POWER temperatures read cold; that is why the station temperatures drive ETo. CIMIS is a California network and does not apply in BC. Risk days (frost, heat) still use POWER Tmax/Tmin and therefore overstate frost and understate heat here.

water_use.note: 100 x clamp(1 - I/I_max); I_max = 412 mm = largest I (high end) among this location's strategies, default years (our choice; spec does not define I_max). rule of thumb, not a model

forage_value.note: 100 x sum(rating/4 x months in field/12 x min(yield/10000,1)) / cycle_years, over harvested forage crops. Months in field replaces the count of harvest months (that count scored a one-cut silage crop below a multi-cut hay of similar dry matter). Range = rating and yield ranges (both assumed). rule of thumb, not a model

n_fixation.note: 100 x sum(rating_nfix/4 x months growing/12)/cycle_years, legumes only; ratings assumed, range = rating range. rule of thumb, not a model

erosion.note: Relative to today's rotation: 100 x E_baseline / (E_baseline + E). Today's rotation = 50; less rain-weighted bare exposure scores above 50 (no exposure = 100), more scores below 50 (twice today's = 33). Not clamped. Change in E vs today: +0.0%. The 30% residue-rating blend was dropped from the score (it made today's rotation score non-zero and mixed an absolute rating into a relative score); it is reported as residue_component. rule of thumb, not a model

exposure_component.note: 100 x (1 - E/E_baseline), NOT clamped: 0 for today's rotation, negative = more rain-weighted bare exposure than today; null if E_baseline = 0

residue_component.note: 100 x lasting_residue/4, crop-day mean rating. Shown for context, not part of the erosion score: residue would belong inside the cover term (RUSLE soil-loss-ratio subfactors, USDA Agriculture Handbook 703), which needs daily residue cover we do not have

slope_pct.note: Salmon River valley-floor hay field placeholder (assumed); the NASADEM slope is pending (backend/nasa_open terrain not run for BC). Cancels in E/E_baseline.

organic_matter.note: soil_builder 3.00, lasting_residue 1.00 (crop-day means), perennial years 1.00/1. Range = bare threshold/rain/precip combos and the rating ranges. rule of thumb, not a model

market.note: 50 +/- 25 by share of products matching 'no_preference' (sell: rice/hay/wheat; feed: silage/sorghum-sudan). Base 50 and the linear rule are ours. No uncertainty model. Always a local-review item. rule of thumb, not a model

pest_break.note: Adjusted formula: 100 x min(1, distinct families/3) x min(1, extra host-free years / 3). Host = today's main crop (Alfalfa hay, 2 cuts, irrigated (Shuswap)); extra host-free years = (longest circular stretch without the host - today's) / 365, so today's rotation scores 0 and the normal winter gap earns nothing. 3 years for a full break from UC IPM alfalfa ('a 3- to 4-year nonhost crop rotation is ideal'); range 2-4 years; using it for rice is our assumption; UC IPM rice (https://ipm.ucanr.edu/agriculture/rice/integrated-weed-management/) names cereals, safflower and dry fallow as rotations out of rice. Families ['Fabaceae']; longest stretch without Alfalfa hay, 2 cuts, irrigated (Shuswap) 0 d vs 0 d today = 0.00 extra host-free years. No pest dataset exists. rule of thumb, not a model

infiltration.note: compaction 3.00, root class 2.00, cover months 12.0; range = rating/root-class ranges. Hydrologic group unknown (No field-scale soil API in BC like SSURGO; SoilGrids v2 (a 250 m global model) is used instead.). rule of thumb, not a model

n_scavenging.note: 100 x rating/4 x fall-winter cover months/6, computed day by day over Oct-Mar with cover >= 0.5 (6.0 months); ratings assumed, range = rating range. rule of thumb, not a model

income.note: Income not computed (as for the California fields): NASS/AMS do not cover BC and no BC yield-price series is wired in. Hay price stand-in: about 336 CAD/t (211-476), from California AMS prices (estimate, see price_range). Seed cost alone (assumed) would be ~300 USD/ha/yr.

price_range.note: ESTIMATE, California stand-in: USDA AMS California hay report (slug 2904), North Inter-Mountains region, F.O.B. weighted-average prices for Alfalfa, Alfalfa/Orchard Mix, Alfalfa/Grass Mix, 2021-2025 (362 quotes): median 222 USD/short ton (10th-90th percentile 140-315). Converted at an assumed 1.37 CAD per USD (about the Bank of Canada 2024 annual average, 1.3698; rate as of 2024, not checked for Nov 2026) and 0.907185 t per short ton. Not a BC price: no BC hay price series is wired in.

seed_cost_per_ha.note: Sum of crop seed-cost placeholders per cycle year

local_review.item: Every alternative rotation needs review by the grower and an adviser before anything is seeded.

Market suitability is a table rule: confirm buyers, contracts, equipment and the field's water licence terms under BC's Water Sustainability Act (including fish population protection orders such as the Aug 2023 Salmon River order) locally.
Kamloops District Forage Manual system 1: continuous alfalfa, 5-year cycle, 20% reseeded each year. Modelled as one established stand in steady state.

not_available_in_bc.cimis: CIMIS is California's station network; BC has two ECCC climate stations near this field (one closed in 2021).
not_available_in_bc.insurance: USDA RMA crop-insurance records cover the United States only; BC Production Insurance loss data is not public at field or county level.
not_available_in_bc.sgma: SGMA, water districts and CDEC reservoirs are California institutions; BC water licensing is not integrated.
not_available_in_bc.cdl: No USDA Cropland Data Layer in Canada; AAFC's Annual Crop Inventory is used instead (one Pasture / Forages class, no alfalfa class).
not_available_in_bc.soil_survey: No field-scale soil API in BC like SSURGO; SoilGrids v2 (a 250 m global model) is used instead.
not_available_in_bc.outlook: The coming-season outlooks (NOAA CPC, US Drought Monitor, CDEC) are US products; not built for BC.
not_available_in_bc.ml_calendar: The machine-learning calendar and stress models were trained on California fields and were not run here.

pest_break.note: Adjusted formula: 100 x min(1, distinct families/3) x min(1, extra host-free years / 3). Host = today's main crop (Alfalfa hay, 2 cuts, irrigated (Shuswap)); extra host-free years = (longest circular stretch without the host - today's) / 365, so today's rotation scores 0 and the normal winter gap earns nothing. 3 years for a full break from UC IPM alfalfa ('a 3- to 4-year nonhost crop rotation is ideal'); range 2-4 years; using it for rice is our assumption; UC IPM rice (https://ipm.ucanr.edu/agriculture/rice/integrated-weed-management/) names cereals, safflower and dry fallow as rotations out of rice. Families ['Fabaceae', 'Poaceae']; Alfalfa hay, 2 cuts, irrigated (Shuswap) never grown in the modelled cycle (counted as a full break; the real break depends on the years around it). No pest dataset exists. rule of thumb, not a model

infiltration.note: compaction 3.00, root class 2.00, cover months 12.0; range = rating/root-class ranges. Hydrologic group unknown (No field-scale soil API in BC like SSURGO; SoilGrids v2 (a 250 m global model) is used instead.). rule of thumb, not a model

n_scavenging.note: 100 x rating/4 x fall-winter cover months/6, computed day by day over Oct-Mar with cover >= 0.5 (6.0 months); ratings assumed, range = rating range. rule of thumb, not a model

income.note: Income not computed (as for the California fields): NASS/AMS do not cover BC and no BC yield-price series is wired in. Hay price stand-in: about 336 CAD/t (211-476), from California AMS prices (estimate, see price_range). Seed cost alone (assumed) would be ~250 USD/ha/yr.

price_range.note: ESTIMATE, California stand-in: USDA AMS California hay report (slug 2904), North Inter-Mountains region, F.O.B. weighted-average prices for Alfalfa, Alfalfa/Orchard Mix, Alfalfa/Grass Mix, 2021-2025 (362 quotes): median 222 USD/short ton (10th-90th percentile 140-315). Converted at an assumed 1.37 CAD per USD (about the Bank of Canada 2024 annual average, 1.3698; rate as of 2024, not checked for Nov 2026) and 0.907185 t per short ton. Not a BC price: no BC hay price series is wired in.

seed_cost_per_ha.note: Sum of crop seed-cost placeholders per cycle year

local_review.item: Every alternative rotation needs review by the grower and an adviser before anything is seeded.

Market suitability is a table rule: confirm buyers, contracts, equipment and the field's water licence terms under BC's Water Sustainability Act (including fish population protection orders such as the Aug 2023 Salmon River order) locally.
Sainfoin + meadow brome hay, dryland, 1 cut: needs lighter, well-drained soil with no wet feet (BF04); check the SoilGrids texture
Sainfoin + meadow brome hay, dryland, 1 cut: BF04 was written for northern BC (Bulkley-Nechako, Fraser-Fort George); its use in the Shuswap is assumed
Sainfoin with a bunchgrass (meadow brome), dryland (BF04). Needs lighter, well-drained soil with no wet feet: check the SoilGrids texture before relying on this option.

not_available_in_bc.openet: OpenET covers the western United States only; there is no field-scale measured water use for BC.
not_available_in_bc.cimis: CIMIS is California's station network; BC has two ECCC climate stations near this field (one closed in 2021).
not_available_in_bc.insurance: USDA RMA crop-insurance records cover the United States only; BC Production Insurance loss data is not public at field or county level.
not_available_in_bc.sgma: SGMA, water districts and CDEC reservoirs are California institutions; BC water licensing is not integrated.
not_available_in_bc.cdl: No USDA Cropland Data Layer in Canada; AAFC's Annual Crop Inventory is used instead (one Pasture / Forages class, no alfalfa class).
not_available_in_bc.soil_survey: No field-scale soil API in BC like SSURGO; SoilGrids v2 (a 250 m global model) is used instead.
not_available_in_bc.outlook: The coming-season outlooks (NOAA CPC, US Drought Monitor, CDEC) are US products; not built for BC.
not_available_in_bc.ml_calendar: The machine-learning calendar and stress models were trained on California fields and were not run here.
